EXAM TRAP   Integration is not the same as interfacing
Two systems that send each other files are interfaced. One system holding one copy of the data is integrated. A question describing nightly file transfers between modules is describing interfaced systems, whatever the vendor calls the product.

WORKED EXAMPLE   The pattern behind the judgement
Integration is worth most to a company whose questions span its systems.
The gain is not the software but the ability to plan from drivers and review in time to act.
The cost is paid in process change and vendor dependence, not only in licence fees.
Heavy customisation destroys the benefit it was bought to protect.

EXAM TRAP   Exam view
A Level C question asks whether performance management helps, or what it makes possible. Name the mechanism, not the benefit: driver-based planning, continuous forecasting, plan and actual together, and review feeding the next plan. Answering that it improves decisions earns nothing.
